name: Original retrieval rerun (post region-match + discovery-routing fixes)

factual_named.verdict: Unchanged — metric mismatch persists (expected, P@5 wrong for factual lookup)

interpretation: The region-matching bug fix and discovery-intent routing improved exploratory retrieval by +0.171 P@5 (0.600 → 0.771), pushing it ABOVE the pre-registered threshold of 0.70. This validates the hypothesis that the original low score was partly due to the region-matching bug (cross-region leaks like Wadi Wishwashi) and that discovery queries benefit from explicit intent routing. The aggregate P@5 remains below threshold (0.387 < 0.70) because the factual_named bucket (where P@5 is the wrong metric) continues to score ~0 — confirming the pathway-aware interpretation from the original snapshot.
thesis_ch4_update: Report BOTH snapshots side-by-side: original (pre-fix) 0.307 and post-fix 0.387, with exploratory stratification showing 0.600 → 0.771 crossing the threshold. This strengthens the thesis narrative: diagnostic insight → informed engineering iteration → measurable improvement on the correct pathway.
caveats: LLM nondeterminism: chat-path responses vary run-to-run, but retrieval_top5 (what P@5 measures) is deterministic — search_pois is a deterministic DB query, not an LLM call.
Labelling rubric is deterministic/rule-based (no LLM judge) for reproducibility, same as original snapshot interpretation.
Original snapshot did not compute per-type nDCG@5; post-fix adds this metric for completeness.
n=3 for factual_compare and n=1 for offtopic are too small for statistical significance.
